title: Special effects and green screens
examples: What is the difference between CGI and practical effects?
Can you show me how a chroma key works in action?
What are some famous examples of special effects in movies?

explain.say: Today we are learning about special effects in movies. These effects make films look amazing. We will look at three main types of effects.

draw.text: Types of Film Effects: Chroma Key, CGI, Practical

explain.say: First we look at chroma key. This technique uses a solid coloured background. The background is usually green or blue. This colour is called the chroma key.
Next we explore CGI. CGI stands for computer generated imagery. This means the images are created using computer software. It allows for things that are impossible in real life.
Our third type is practical effects. These are physical effects made on set. Think of things like fake smoke or real costumes. They are tangible and used in the actual filming.
Consider a scene where a spaceship lands in a forest. The chroma key removes the green screen. CGI creates the spaceship model. Practical effects might add real smoke around the landing site.
A common mistake is thinking all special effects are computer made. Remember that practical effects add real depth to the film. They make the fake parts feel more real to the camera.

faq.q: How exactly does the chroma key process work?
faq.a: The chroma key software identifies the specific colour of the screen. It then digitally removes that colour from the picture. It replaces the removed colour with a different background image.
asks: What is the green screen trick?
How do they make the background disappear?

faq.q: Is CGI always better than practical effects?
faq.a: No, they are different tools for different jobs. Practical effects are great for things that need to feel heavy or real. CGI is better for things that are too big or small to build.
asks: Can I use both CGI and practical?

faq.q: What colours work best for a green screen?
faq.a: The best colours are those that do not appear naturally on the actors or costumes. Green and blue are very common choices for this reason.
asks: What colour should I use for my screen?
Are there other colours besides green?

faq.q: What is the difference between CGI and digital effects?
faq.a: CGI is the overall process of creating images with computers. Digital effects are a broader term that includes CGI, but also things like digital makeup.
asks: Are digital effects the same as CGI?
Does CGI cover all computer work?

faq.q: Do they need a lot of time to make these effects?
faq.a: Yes, both CGI and chroma key work require many hours of careful editing. Practical effects still need time for building and filming on set.
asks: Is it fast or slow to make these?

facts: Chroma key relies on a specific, uniform background colour.
CGI allows filmmakers to create entirely imaginary worlds.
Practical effects involve physical models, costumes, or makeup.
The green or blue colour must not match anything in the scene.

quiz.say: When a film shows a giant alien creature that was never built, which effect is most likely used?
quiz.why: CGI allows artists to build and animate creatures that do not exist in the real world.

wrong.1: This effect only changes the background colour, not the main subject.
wrong.2: Practical effects must be physically built and filmed on the actual set.
wrong.3: All three techniques can be used to create large creatures.

quiz.say: If a scene uses smoke that drifts across the floor, what effect is being used?
quiz.why: Smoke is a physical element that can be generated on set using real machines.

wrong.1: Chroma key is only for changing backgrounds.
wrong.2: While CGI can add smoke, physical smoke is often more realistic.
wrong.3: This question specifically asks about a physical element, not a background change.

quiz.say: What is the primary purpose of using a blue screen?
quiz.show: To isolate a specific colour for replacement
quiz.why: The blue screen is a tool used specifically for the chroma key process to remove the background.

wrong.1: CGI is the creation of the image, not the background removal tool itself.
wrong.2: Practical effects are physical objects, not coloured screens.
wrong.3: The goal is removal and replacement, not just adding colour.
